author: reek
body: THE KEY TYPE IS THE ONLY THING BETWEEN THESE BYTES AND THE WRONG ALGORITHM. Each arm of the dispatch checks xk-alg before it uses the key, and with the parser's own output that check is redundant: an RSA key has no point in xk-bytes and an EC key has no modulus, so the arithmetic refuses on width whichever arm it lands in. Measured, not assumed -- deleting either check moved nothing at all.

author: reek
body: So the type is crossed with the MATERIAL here. Each key below carries the genuine bytes of one algorithm under the label of the other, which is the one state that tells the two rejections apart: with the check, refused because the label is wrong; without it, the signature verifies perfectly because the material is right.

author: reek
body: Nothing the parser can emit looks like this today. That is the point of writing it down: the check costs one line and it is what stops a later key type, or a reused field, from becoming a signature checked under an algorithm nobody agreed to.

author: reek
body: Every scheme the ClientHello offers must be one this verifier accepts. The two sets are written in two places -- tls-ext-sig-algs in Tls and the dispatch in TlsCert -- and nothing else makes them agree.
